## Summary

If the applicant does not file a counter statement within **two months from receiving the copy of the notice of opposition**, the applicant is **deemed to have abandoned the trade mark application** under Section 21(2) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

The Registry may then issue an order recording the abandonment. The supplied draft manual states that the counter statement is filed in **Form TM-6**, subject to the prescribed fee and verification requirements.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

> “If he does not do so he shall be deemed to have abandoned his application.”

Source: Section 21(2), Trade Marks Act, 1999.

## Summary

Under the supplied text of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015:

- Designated persons and their immediate relatives must not trade in securities when the trading window is closed.
- The compliance officer may close the trading window when a designated person or class of designated persons can reasonably be expected to possess unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI).
- A trading restriction period applies from the end of every quarter until 48 hours after the declaration of the financial results.
- Therefore, the restriction around quarterly results is not stated as a fixed number of calendar days. It runs from the quarter-end date through the end of the 48-hour period after results are declared.

The text also states that the restriction applies to the securities to which the relevant UPSI relates. Certain specified transactions and bona fide pledges may be exempt, subject to the stated pre-clearance and regulatory conditions.

## Relevant quotation

“Designated persons and their immediate relatives shall not trade in securities when the trading window is closed.”

“Trading restriction period shall be made applicable from the end of every quarter till 48 hours after the declaration of financial results.”

## Summary

Under section 16 of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person must generally satisfy these conditions before taking input tax credit:

- The goods or services must be used, or intended to be used, in the course or furtherance of business.
- The person must possess:
  - a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under the CGST Act, or
  - another prescribed tax-paying document.
- The invoice or debit-note details must have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient.
- The registered person must have received the goods or services.
- The credit must be taken subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions and in the manner specified in section 49.
- Under section 41, eligible input tax credit is self-assessed in the return and is credited provisionally to the electronic credit ledger.

For deemed receipt, the evidence states that goods may be treated as received where they are delivered to the recipient or another person on the registered person’s direction. Services may be treated as received where supplied to a person on the registered person’s direction and account.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

Section 16(2) provides that no registered person is entitled to credit unless:

> “he is in possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under this Act, or such other tax paying documents as may be prescribed”

and

> “he has received the goods or services or both.”

cases.answer:
## Summary

Under section 16 of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person must generally satisfy these conditions before taking input tax credit (ITC):

- The goods or services must be used, or intended to be used, in the course or furtherance of business.
- The person must possess:
  - a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under the CGST Act, or
  - another prescribed tax-paying document.
- The invoice or debit-note details must have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient in the prescribed manner.
- The registered person must have received the goods or services.
- The ITC must be claimed subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions, in the manner specified under section 49.
- The eligible ITC is self-assessed in the return and credited on a provisional basis to the electronic credit ledger.

Receipt may be deemed to occur in certain cases, such as where goods are delivered to the recipient or another person on the registered person’s direction, or services are supplied to a person on the registered person’s direction and account.

The supplied extract does not cover every possible ITC restriction or condition under the Act and Rules. Legal currentness is unverified because the evidence is stated to be amended only up to 1 January 2022. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

Section 16(1) states that credit is available for supplies “which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business.”

Section 16(2) provides that no credit is available unless the registered person has the required tax document, the relevant invoice or debit-note details have been furnished and communicated, and “he has received the goods or services or both.”

## Summary

Based on the supplied extract of section 16 of the CGST Act, a registered person must satisfy these conditions for claiming input tax credit:

- **Business use:** The goods or services must be used, or intended to be used, in the course or furtherance of business.
- **Prescribed conditions and manner:** The credit is subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions and must be taken in the manner specified under section 49.
- **Valid supporting document:** The person must possess a tax invoice or debit note issued by a supplier registered under the CGST Act, or another prescribed tax-paying document.
- **Supplier reporting and communication:** The invoice or debit-note details must have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies and communicated to the recipient in the prescribed manner under section 37.
- **Receipt of supply:** The person must have received the goods or services. The extract also provides deemed-receipt rules for certain directed deliveries or services.
- **Claim in the return:** Under the supplied extract of section 41, eligible input tax credit is self-assessed and claimed in the person’s return, subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

This summary is based only on the supplied text, which is stated to reflect the law up to **1 January 2022**. Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.
